notes.summary: The exact full envelope has an F-sigma meagre strict regularization defect whenever its competitor family is nonempty. Scalar defect height is bounded by that base defect. This does not prove analytic removability or normal sufficiency.
notes.detailedSummary: For every usc obstacle, either the globally real-valued competitor family is empty and both envelopes are minus infinity, or a fixed continuous competitor supplies a baseline. In the nonempty case the raw envelope s is finite lsc, u=s* is finite usc, and h0<=s<=u<=f. The defect {s<u} is exactly the discontinuity set of s and is a countable union of closed nowhere-dense sets. For any continuous surjection q, v=(s composed with q)* satisfies s composed with q<=v<=u composed with q. If q is closed with compact fibers, u(x)=max over the fiber of v. These facts do not identify a freshly extended competitor family or establish any positive classification.
notes.text:
Let U be a good separated strict analytic domain over a complete nontrivially valued field. For an usc obstacle f:U->R union {-infinity}, let E be the entire globally real-valued locally-Fubini–Study/semipositive-real-PL minorant union, s=sup E, and u(x)=inf over ordinary open neighborhoods N containing x of sup_N s. At the actual GJR definitions, real PL functions are finite continuous, and LFS functions are real PL with semiample residue classes. Thus every competitor is continuous. No invariant, rational, equicontinuous or selected-family restriction is imposed.

If E is empty, s=u=-infinity under the required convention. A single point where f=-infinity already forces E empty, because every competitor is globally real-valued. In the nonempty case choose h0 in E. Upper semicontinuity and the absence of +infinity make f locally bounded above, so h0<=s<=u<=f and s,u are finite. To prove u<=f, take a neighborhood where f<f(x)+epsilon and apply the neighborhood formula, then let epsilon decrease to zero. Also {s>t}=union over h in E of {h>t}, so s is lsc.

For rationals a<b define A_ab={s<=a} intersect {u>=b}. These sets are closed. They have empty interior: if a nonempty open W were contained in A_ab, then s<=a on W would imply u<=a at every point of W, contradicting u>=b. Hence each A_ab is nowhere dense. Every strict gap contains rationals s(x)<a<b<u(x), and membership in A_ab implies a gap. Therefore {s<u}=union_{a<b in Q} A_ab. If s is continuous at x, then u(x)=s(x). Conversely equality supplies a local upper bound s<s(x)+epsilon from regularization and a local lower bound s>s(x)-epsilon from lsc, proving continuity. Consequently the strict defect is exactly the discontinuity set of s, is F-sigma and meagre, and has dense G-delta complement because locally compact Hausdorff U is Baire. This includes relative-boundary points. No conclusion follows about the closure of the defect being proper.

For a continuous surjection q:Y->U put v=(s composed with q)*. Regularization majorizes its raw input. Pulling back a base neighborhood gives v(y)<=u(q(y)); the pulled continuous baseline makes v finite. Thus 0<=u(q(y))-v(y)<=u(q(y))-s(q(y)). The strict upstairs defect lies over {s<u}, and equality holds on every fiber over a continuity point of s.

If q is also closed with compact fibers, v attains a finite maximum m on q^{-1}(x), and m<=u(x). If m<u(x), choose m<t<u(x). Each fiber point has an open neighborhood where s composed with q<t. A finite union N covers the compact fiber. Closedness gives the base neighborhood W=U minus q(Y minus N), whose entire inverse image lies in N. Surjectivity gives s<t on W and therefore u(x)<=t, a contradiction. Hence u(x)=max_{q(y)=x}v(y).

For scalar maps this concerns the pulled ground-field raw family only. No cofinality with the newly defined upstairs family is proved. Meagreness does not imply removability, and a nonopen projection can give its inverse image interior. No classical positivity, CLD-v2 conclusion, general continuity result, or sharp normal/geometrically-unibranch classification follows. These are continuum proofs, not finite computational observations.

The complete arguments are in argument.md Sections 1–3 and P03.1-paper.tex. Exact sources and retained bodies are recorded in input-bindings.json and source-extracts/. Rerun from this directory with python run_all.py; its programs are independently owned standard-library programs.

notes.summary: A bounded continuous-family supremum can have dense meagre defect, and a compact proper surjection with connected fibers and a continuous section can turn that into an open upstairs defect. This is a topological diagnostic, not an analytic P03.1 counterexample.
notes.detailedSummary: Enumerate rational q_n in [0,1], set s(q_n)=-1/n and s=0 at irrationals. Then s is lsc, s*=0, and s is the increasing supremum of continuous Lipschitz inf-convolutions. Attach a hair of height 1/n at each rational and project the compact resulting space onto the interval. Fibers are compact connected; projection is closed, proper and surjective, with a continuous section at which it is locally open. Upstairs regularization equals zero on the section and -1/n at positive height on the nth hair. The strict defect is a nonempty open subset upstairs. The continuous retraction realizes the fiber maximum without making the regularization fiberwise constant.
notes.text:
Enumerate the distinct rational numbers of X=[0,1] as q_1,q_2,..., ordered by increasing reduced denominator and then numerator, starting with 0 and 1. Define s(q_n)=-1/n and s(x)=0 at irrational x. For t<0 the sublevel {s<=t} is finite or empty; for t>=0 it is X. Hence s is lsc. Irrationals are dense, so s*=0. The strict defect is the countable dense rational set, demonstrating that the meagre defect in n1 can have full closure.

This s is a supremum of bounded continuous functions. For integers m>=1 define b_m(x)=inf_{t in X}(s(t)+m|x-t|). The common Lipschitz bound inside the infimum gives an m-Lipschitz b_m. We have -1<=b_m<=s<=0, and b_m increases with m. Given x and epsilon>0, lower semicontinuity supplies delta>0 such that s(t)>s(x)-epsilon when |t-x|<delta. Outside this radius, s(t)+m|x-t|>=-1+m delta, which eventually exceeds s(x)-epsilon. Thus b_m(x)->s(x), proving s=sup_m b_m.

Let Y=(X times {0}) union the hairs {q_n} times [0,1/n], and let q(x,t)=x. Y is closed in the compact square: a convergent sequence using unbounded indices has heights tending to zero, while positive limiting height restricts to finitely many hairs. Hence Y is compact Hausdorff and q is continuous, closed, surjective and proper. Every fiber is connected, being a singleton or an interval. The section sigma(x)=(x,0) is continuous. Every neighborhood of a section point contains nearby base points, so its image contains a neighborhood of x: projection is open at section points in this neighborhood-image sense.

At (q_n,t) with t>0, choose a neighborhood meeting only the nth hair. Hairs with sufficiently large index have height less than t/2; avoid the finitely many other remaining horizontal coordinates and the base. On that neighborhood s composed with q=-1/n. Consequently v=(s composed with q)*=-1/n there. At a base point every neighborhood contains base points with irrational coordinate, so v(x,0)=0. Therefore v(x,0)=0, v(q_n,t)=-1/n for t>0, and s* composed with q=0 everywhere. The strict upstairs defect is exactly Y minus (X times {0}), a nonempty open subset whose image is the meagre rational defect downstairs.

The fiber maximum is zero and is attained by the section. The continuous idempotent retraction r=sigma composed with q satisfies v composed with r=s* composed with q=0, although v is not constant on rational fibers. Thus connected compact fibers, a continuous section, openness at section points, a fiber-maximum identity and continuous retraction topology do not alone prove scalar compatibility. This agrees with the inequalities proved in n1.

The functions b_m have not been shown analytic psh, LFS or real PL, and Y is not asserted to be an analytic scalar-extension space. This is not a residual normal/geometrically-unibranch counterexample and supplies no analytic removability theorem. Its proof is a continuum argument, not a finite search. It is retained in argument.md Section 3a and P03.1-paper.tex. Reproduce the artifacts with python run_all.py.

notes.summary: The requested paper, scope/source/coverage records and rerunnable evidence were produced. Original P03.1 remains unresolved: no general normal or geometrically-unibranch sufficiency or every-extension curve theorem was established.
notes.detailedSummary: The self-contained draft contains n1–n2 and explicit reconstructions of the required split-branch, nonsplit-node/open-disc and codimension-two pinching obstructions. Those examples do not settle the residual everywhere-unibranch range. The finite-maxima approach fails because its pointwise limit is s, while GR1 Theorem 6.5 requires an already-usc actual limit. The scalar analytic step remains unproved. Source hashes, compilation and exact finite diagnostics establish reproducibility, not mathematical correctness. The original classification is incomplete and candidate=false.
notes.text:
Original-scope decision: incomplete, candidate=false. Classical psh requires analytic-curve tests after EVERY complete analytic extension. No general theorem here proves those tests for s* on arbitrary normal higher-dimensional affinoids or geometrically unibranch domains. The result n1 bounds the defect without removing it; n2 shows why the continuous-section topological route is insufficient. Neither a meagre defect nor a dense defect-free G-delta set is a removability theorem.

The draft records explicit reconstructions of the required necessity phenomena. Sections 4–6 give the split-node/product construction, a bounded strict quotient presentation of the pinched bidisc with its height-two point and full-envelope spike, and the Q3 nonsplit-node/open-disc construction with a continuous obstacle, integral-binomial rational LFS witnesses and a genuine quadratic-extension disc test. These are reconstructed supplied examples outside the residual everywhere-geometrically-unibranch class. They are not new normal counterexamples or a complete classification. The pinching argument proves affine-algebra seminormality without asserting a freshly verified analytic-stalk comparison. Actual relative-boundary and interior requirements are distinguished throughout.

The finite-maxima attempt has a precise gap. Its directed pointwise limit is the raw s. GR1 Theorem 6.5 assumes that the actual limit is already usc; it does not permit replacing s by s* at a strict defect point. Maxima are not assumed real PL across irrational walls. The supplied graph-tube body was inspected as DATA: after extension it controls (s composed with pi)*, whereas the required tests use s* composed with pi. No scalar equality, analytic section, arbitrary scalar orbit presentation, finite-flat scalar presentation, globalization cofinality, or subharmonicity-preserving retraction has been proved. The empty-family minus-infinity convention is retained. P03.2 and P03.3 remain separate and unclaimed.

Deliverables are P03.1-paper.tex, the compiled nine-page P03.1-paper.pdf, argument.md, exact-scope.md, source-application-ledger.md, whole-proof-coverage.md, original-scope-and-noncircularity-decision.md, native-notes.json, input-bindings.json, own-bindings.json, environment.json, input-bindings/, source-extracts/ and evidence/. Rerun with python run_all.py. It sequentially runs the owned prepare_evidence.py, diagnostics.py, build_artifacts.py, make_notes.py and check_artifacts.py. Supplied programs were neither executed nor imported. No agents, external editor actions, publication, catalogue mutation, environment override or heavy computation occurred.

Actual execution evidence: all nine frozen mathematical DATA files and ten primary manifest files matched their specified hashes, totaling 24,647,011 bytes. Four inspected referenced book bodies were also retained as ungranted data. Nine literal source excerpts were retained. Both TeX passes exited 0; the PDF is 215,203 bytes and the final build reported no layout warnings. Exact polynomial diagnostics gave zero residuals for V^2-SV-S^3, J^2-ZJ-SZ^2 and VZ-SJ. All 33 tested binomial coefficients were 3-adic integral, and (1+t)B(t)^2=1 was checked through degree 32. These finite checks do not prove the infinite identity, analytic convergence, geometry or envelope positivity. Administrative checks found 15 required deliverables, 25 bound input records and an acyclic n1–n3 support graph.

The environment was Python 3.12.14 on Linux-6.18.44-x86_64-with-glibc2.41.
